UNCITED EDGE THRESHOLDS: No empirical justification given for the sizing-map thresholds themselves (0.70 full, 0.50 half, <0.50 starter). The definition cites backtest wins (score-9 realised 0.774, tier-monotonicity restoration) but does NOT justify why a 0.70 win-rate earns 'full' — did the team backtest sizing regrets at 0.65 vs 0.70? This is referenced only as 'from 0.65 → 0.70 after Phase 3 quintile data' but no quintile win-rate table is shown.

FALLBACK PROXY LOGIC OPACITY: Lines 18–23 detail a cascading fallback when uw historical signal-backtest returns empty. The fallback reads rolling 'conviction_<date>' watchlists from the last 30 calendar days, matches realised WIN/LOSS per ticker, and computes empirical win-rate. But 'rolling conviction watchlists' are ephemeral; no spec for how they are versioned or archived. If a ticker was flagged HIGH on 2026-06-10 but the watchlist was purged, the fallback cannot reconstruct it. This fallback feels like a 'just-in-case' that may brittle in practice.

DOUBLE-GATING AMBIGUITY: Accumulation names can be gated twice (C11 conjunction halves +3 to +1 on weak flow; flow_conflict deductions then apply separately on the same name). The text claims 'both mechanisms may fire on the same ticker' and 'that is intended' — but the sum of −1 flow_conflict_lite + reduced +1 accumulation is a net −0 swing on a badly-confirmed name, easily misinterpreted as 'no signal' when it is actually 'signal penalised'. Audit trails must be crystal-clear or users will misunderstand.

BACKTEST SAMPLE SIZE UNDOCUMENTED: The 'uw historical signal-backtest' tool returns 'n' (sample count). The definition tightens the cap from n=10 → 0.69, but does NOT specify how backtest samples are counted. Are they 1-per-ticker-per-date-window, or do multileg combos count fractionally? If 8 bullish_flow signals on a single date and same tickers count as n=8, the cap is too aggressive; if each unique (ticker, date, signal) triple counts separately, n could balloon. Spec is opaque.

MARKET-EXCESS BENCHMARK ISOLATION RULE FRAGILITY: Line 57 says 'Do NOT reuse SPY's appearance *inside* the signal class's own backtest set as the benchmark — that conflates the signal with its reference.' This is correct in principle, but operationally: the signal class's backtest windows and the SPY benchmark windows must align exactly (same dates, same event boundaries). If the tools return incompatible window specs, the excess computation silently degrades. No error handling is specified.

INTENT-SCREEN DEFINITION VAGUE ON DIVIDEND-CAPTURE ARBS: Line 24 flags 'no C28 distribution_flag; no deep-ITM sub-parity ex-div call prints on dividend payers'. The 'deep-ITM sub-parity' phrase is domain jargon (likely used by the team internally) but is not precisely defined. What ITM threshold qualifies? How is 'sub-parity' detected in option data? The NEE 2026-06-04 example is pointed, but the rule is too implicit for re-implementation.

TIER INVERSION COMMENT ABOUT IN-SAMPLE BIAS: Line 127 says '⚠️ In-sample-only — re-confirm at the ~2026-06-12 audit' and notes the 2026-05-30 holdout had zero resolved HIGH calls and the dataset is a single UPTREND regime. The 0.80 average win-rate for score-9 is thus not out-of-sample. The team itself flags this as provisional, yet the agent definition enshrines the 9-point cut as THE tier boundary without a plan for what happens if the 2026-06-12 reconfirm fails.

FLOW_CONFLICT UNION-MEDIAN OPERATIONALLY VAGUE: Line 106 says 'if |cum_flow_30d| > today's union-median |cum_flow_30d|' — but 'today's union' is the union passed by the orchestrator. If the union is small (e.g., 5 names), the median is brittle. If a union is recomputed mid-market, medians shift. The 'mechanical $50M magnitude alternative phrasing' at line 116 acknowledges this fragility ('may be used when union-median is unavailable'). The primary rule is operationally fragile.

LOAD-BEARING TOOL LIST HARDCODED WITHOUT DEPRECATION PROCESS: The 5 load-bearing tools (dark-pool block-stratified, cum-premium-flow, institutional-accumulation, dex, signal-confluence) are presented as fixed. But the same document repeatedly patches these tools (cum-premium-flow demoted to +1, signal-confluence demoted on swing, sweep-persistence deprecated). What is the process for re-evaluating the LB-gate toolset? If a tool is NO-INFO on the next audit, does it drop from the 3-of-5 immediately, or does it remain in the gate (making HIGH calls unjustly demote)?

ABSOLUTE CEILING 0.80 NEVER QUOTED >0.80 — TRUE FOR EDGE CLAIMS?: Line 51 says 'the 0.80–0.90 quote bucket realised 62%, the ≥0.90 bucket realised 53%' — these are *realised* win-rates on *historical* calls. But the 0.80 cap is applied prospectively to new backtest results. Does the historical underperformance at 0.80–0.90 imply that 0.80-quoted calls will underperform in the future, or was it a one-time sample artifact? This is presented as a hard mechanical rule, but the statistical justification is weak.

FRACTIONAL KELLY GATED BUT NOT REMOVED: Lines 70–71 describe a Kelly sizer that is 'ADVISORY until n≥30' and 'do not change pre_risk_size off Kelly while gate is ADVISORY.' This creates a temporal dependency: the agent may emit advisory Kelly fields, but must still use the win-rate ladder. On a re-run, if /calibration-audit later updates the Kelly gate status, the old envelopes with Kelly fields become inconsistent (they were sized off the ladder, but now appear to have Kelly info). This design invites silent inconsistency in the audit trail.

AUDIT-TRAIL PROSE MUST EQUAL NUMERIC COMPONENTS: Line 155 says 'Σ score_components.points MUST mechanically equal raw_score.' This is correct, but the 195-line definition contains many conditional branches (conjunction gates, market-excess downgrades, mutual-exclusivity rules). If an agent misses even one branch (e.g. applies flow_conflict AND flow_conflict_lite on the same name), the Σ diverges and the audit fails *after* the score is already computed. The definition should require a pre-emit validation step (e.g., a schema check function) rather than relying on per-agent discipline.

BEHAVIORAL BIAS: Agent definition is labeled 'desk quant who owns the conviction score' but references at least 9 prior audits and multiple register updates. The tone suggests an iteratively-refined tool, not a specification. Teams tend to over-fit to recent audit results. Is the 0.69 cap for n<10 a fundamental principle or a fit to one week's data?

LANE BOUNDARY NOT ENFORCED: The definition says 'Stay in your lane: produce the audited number, not the gate.' But the agent is instructed to apply market-excess gates, liquidity floors, OI-opening gates, and conjunctions — all of which reshape the output. These are gates. Risk-monitor is supposed to apply regime/correlation gates, but the boundary between 'quantitative due diligence' (what signal-confluence-quant does) and 'risk gating' (what risk-monitor does) is muddled. A risk-monitor that sees a name already capped at 'half' by market-excess may apply a second downgrade, double-penalizing beta-longs.

NO EXPLICIT ERROR RECOVERY FOR MALFORMED UW OUTPUT: If uw returns an inconsistent result (e.g., signal-confluence returns no dominant_signal_class, or backtest returns negative n), the definition does not specify how to handle it. It only covers empty backtest results (fallback to proxy). A malformed response from an upstream tool leaves the agent undefined.

PHASE TERMINOLOGY CONFUSION: The definition says 'Phase 2 quantitative scoring engine' but also mentions 'Phase 1 candidate union,' 'Phase 2,' 'Phase 3,' 'Phase 4,' 'Phase 5,' and even '/calibration-audit' phases. This agent is scoped to Phase 2, but it consumes outputs from Phase 1 and feeds into risk-monitor (presumably Phase 2 or later). The relationship to the broader agent fleet phases is not clear.

Cross-references earnings-surprise streak, insider MSPR, growth/leverage, news catalyst stack against thesis direction. Emits per-ticker fundamentals_verdict (CONFIRM/CAUTION/VETO/NA), tier_adjustment, earnings_trend, insider_signal, next_earnings_date, catalyst_support, key_risks.

invariants: Σ score_components.points == raw_score (per validate_decision.py line 119-120: total = sum(c.get('points', 0) for c in comps); if total != raw: error)
tier must not exceed band implied by raw_score; demotion OK (per validate_decision.py line 124-125 and _band_max_tier function lines 36-43: HIGH band ≥9, MEDIUM band ≥7, LOW band ≥3, DROP <3)
kelly_fraction (if present) must be in [0, 1] — capped half-Kelly floored at 0 (per validate_decision.py line 136-138)
schema.scored_vs_advisory_fields: SCORED: calls[] array with raw_score, tier, score_components each containing rubric_line, points, source_agent, source_tool, evidence — these scores feed conviction rubric and backtest-weighted sizing. ADVISORY (0 points, out of calls[] by design): next_session_gex (lines 119-150, prose-only dealer-gamma map for SPY/QQQ), next_session_0dte_setup (lines 87-117, delta-neutral premium-selling setup with advisory const true), breadth_cross_check (lines 41-54, fz edge cross-check marked advisory:true, contributes 0 points), fz_context (lines 56-71, Finviz fundamentals ADVISORY per A1/A5 gate status, contributes 0 to raw_score), distribution_flag (lines 73-85, institutional OI distribution counter-signal contributes 0 to raw_score and 0 to tier_adjustment per C28 schema_version>=1.2). The separation is structural: advisory objects cannot enter score_components and are explicitly annotated with "advisory": true or "contributes 0 points" in descriptions.
red_flags: schema_version must be exactly '1.0', '1.1', or '1.2' per enum (line 10)
report_date must match ISO 8601 YYYY-MM-DD pattern (line 11)
report_kind enum constrains to 'daily' or 'weekly' (line 12)
horizon in calls[] is enum-constrained ['0DTE', 'swing', 'LEAP', 'weekly', 'vol'] (line 157)
direction is enum ['long', 'short', 'vol_long', 'vol_short', 'neutral'] (line 159)
tier is enum ['HIGH', 'MEDIUM', 'LOW', 'DROP'] (line 160)
final_size must be one of ['full', 'half', 'starter', 'skip', 'veto', 'watch_only'] (line 185)
fundamentals_verdict enum ['CONFIRM', 'CAUTION', 'VETO', 'NA', null] (line 199)
debate_residual_confidence if present must be exactly one of [0.55, 0.65, 0.75, 0.85, 0.95, null] per enum (line 202)
next_session_gex and next_session_0dte_setup indices constrain symbol to ['SPY', 'QQQ'] only to enforce §2 scope (lines 103, 135)
macro_event_risk impact enum ['high', 'medium', 'low'] (line 26)
additionalProperties: false is enforced across all objects (no extra fields allowed)
